# DoNext Cardiff · orange identity v4

Approved direction: the orange **01 COMPACT** concept, with cream **Do / Next / CARDIFF** lettering. This package uses the supplied production PNG artwork unchanged. It is raster artwork, not a vector or a reconstructed font logo.

## Production assets

All master files are in `C:/Users/MatthewMurray/Documents/Codex/2026-09-04/are/deliverables/donext-brand-v4/`.

| Master | Actual dimensions | Intended use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `donext-cardiff-avatar-v4.png` | 1254 × 1254 | Instagram and Facebook profile image; site brand mark; source for approved favicon sizes |
| `donext-cardiff-share-v4.png` | 1731 × 909 | Site social/link preview image |
| `donext-cardiff-facebook-cover-v4.png` | 2033 × 773 | Facebook Page cover |

Keep these files as the masters. Resize proportionally when required by a destination. Do not stretch, recolour, rebuild the lettering, add icons or illustrations, or replace the city label with live text. Review the destination’s crop before applying. The Facebook cover and link preview are separate compositions and should not be substituted for each other.

Future cities should retain the same design system, but need a newly approved city logo. Do not edit CARDIFF out of this master or generate an unapproved variant automatically.

## Supporting style

- Lead with generous spacing, clear sans-serif typography and short, useful information.
- Use warm ivory (`#FAF7EF`), dark ink (`#20201D`) and a supporting orange (`#F13C08`) around the logo. These are layout colours; do not use them to recolour the PNG.
- Keep the city name visible at profile size. The actual logo lettering is embedded in the master; Arial/Helvetica in the template is supporting typography only.
- Brand line: **Interesting things. For Cardiff kids.** Avoid filling the identity with local landmarks or decorative graphics.

## Future feed posts

Open [instagram-feed-template.html](./instagram-feed-template.html) beside the avatar PNG. It is an editable 1080 × 1350 portrait composition with 78px outer padding. The form updates the artwork and a caption draft locally. No network connection, upload or publishing is performed, and edits are not saved automatically.

Replace **every bracketed placeholder**. Each post needs: what, when (with date), where, ages, cost and a useful details link. Explain one specific reason the event is worth a parent's time. Use verified practical information such as booking, accessibility, duration or suitable ages, rather than generic praise.

The template is deliberately a layout, not a real event or approved post. Keep text concise, resolve any overflow warning, inspect the final composition, then export the graphic to PNG using the team's chosen browser/design workflow. The Print button produces a PDF, not an Instagram-ready image. Review the caption before posting. A URL drawn inside an image does not become a clickable link; make the pick available through the profile’s actual link destination.

Prefer a DoNext pick URL for the public details destination, with official organiser or venue information and booking links on that page. Public source credit should name the organiser or venue. Facebook groups are internal discovery leads: verify against an official source and do not market or credit the groups as the product's source.

Keep the existing editorial selection rules: Cardiff and its nearby area, kids aged 0–12, interesting and local first, free or inexpensive community finds preferred. Familiar tourist attractions are backups unless there is a specific worthwhile new event. Exclude identity/politics-framed events from public kids picks in line with the founder's saved editorial rule. This brand package does not authorise publishing any particular event.

## Production provenance

The built-in ImageGen tool produced the three approved production rasters from the selected orange concept. The exact production prompts and provenance are recorded in [generation-prompts.md](./generation-prompts.md). Prompt intent, summarised:

1. **Avatar:** extract the approved 01 COMPACT orange identity as a square, opaque orange logo, retaining the exact Do / Next / CARDIFF wording and clean composition.
2. **Share card:** a warm ivory composition with the circular orange logo at left, the exact line “Interesting things. For Cardiff kids.”, plus ages 0–12 and `donext.co.uk`.
3. **Facebook cover:** a separate wide composition in the same identity, with generous safe central spacing for the logo and wording.

No new raster images are generated by this handoff or the HTML template. The avatar is embedded as the exact local PNG. Preserve the approved output files when passing the identity to another agent or designer.

## Rollout paths

The website rollout uses the v4 filenames to avoid old cached brand assets:

| Purpose | Intended production path |
| --- | --- |
| Website masthead/footer and declared PNG icon | `/assets/brand/cardiff/donext-cardiff-avatar-v4.png` |
| Open Graph / social preview | `/assets/brand/cardiff/donext-cardiff-share-v4.png` |
| SVG favicon container embedding the approved raster | `/favicon.svg` |
| Touch icon using the approved raster | `/apple-touch-icon.png` |

The website displays the master with a circular CSS crop where appropriate and declares the actual PNG dimensions. The reusable template and this handoff can also live alongside the avatar under `/assets/brand/cardiff/`; their relative image reference works in either location. The Facebook cover is uploaded to the Facebook Page from the local production master and is not required as a website asset.

This file describes asset use; it is not evidence that any website deployment or social profile update has completed. The rollout operator verifies those destinations separately.
